## My request:
Two new PRs:

1. PR: baseline Solenoid around the Tracker (ATLAS style, following PR #8 and respecting its comments), target is a central 3 T field. Make enough space for the solenoid according to the information you had on PR#8.



     Include an RZ-view of the Tracker + Solenoid.



2. PR for Calorimeter: Make an in-depth assessment of the Calorimetric setup of nODD (and its origin the ODD) and point out what is missing to bring it to a similar detailed description as the Tracking detector.



      This first part is really concerning a realistic description

      (support, cryostat, powering, ...) - not yet a realistic performance, which will need also software updates.

I’ll review PR #8 and its comments against the current tracker envelope, then prepare two separate PRs: a solenoid baseline with a tracker-plus-solenoid R–Z view, and a sourced assessment of the calorimeter’s mechanical, material and service gaps.

nODD PR #8 is the RD53 pixel-module proposal. Did you mean the magnet study and expert sizing comments in PR #6? I’ll use those comments as the working reference unless you point me elsewhere.
- Yes, use nODD PR #6
- I meant a different PR #8

The magnet sizing comments are on nODD PR #6; PR #8 is the pixel-module proposal. I’ve asked you to confirm that reference and am continuing with the source review.

The key constraints are explicit cold-mass and vessel spacing, stored-energy sizing, uniform current density in the winding pack, and no active-return solenoid. I’m checking those against today’s tracker extent rather than the older tracker envelope.

Confirmed—I’ll use PR #6. The current tracker host is 1.20 m in radius and extends to |z| = 3.60 m. An initial 7.20 m cold-mass length, with explicit end allowances, is worth checking against the shorter historical coil.

The calorimeter review has already identified a major gap: the maintained nODD entry point currently assembles the beam pipe and tracker. ODD provides detailed calorimeter sampling layers, but not the cassette, cooling, powering and structural inventories needed for comparable hardware detail.

I’m using the PDF skill to check the primary magnet and calorimeter references. I’ll prepare two independent design PRs, with the solenoid sizing calculation and R–Z drawing isolated from the production geometry.

The sizing can fit within the existing 1.64 m radial magnet reservation. The longer tracker requires more axial space: I’m testing a 7.20 m winding and cold mass, with a 7.70 m vessel envelope. That also requires revisiting the calorimeter endcap entrance.

A notable calorimeter issue is the inherited HCAL’s 16 mm “PCB mixture” in every layer. I’ll quantify that material allocation and identify what hardware it represents before proposing changes.

The baseline calculation gives a 1.559 m outer vessel radius and about 143 MJ stored energy, leaving 81 mm inside the 1.64 m reservation. Its numerical controls pass. The R–Z view also shows the field falloff clearly: 3 T at the centre becomes about 1.57 T on axis at the tracker’s axial boundary.

The calorimeter assessment will distinguish the ODD sampling model, the current nODD assembly, and the hardware still needed—especially cassettes, cooling, power, supports and service routes.

Both drafts are written. The solenoid proposal retains the larger engineering reservation and explains the required calorimeter interface changes. The calorimeter report includes a prioritized hardware gap matrix and a staged plan from individual cassettes to full assemblies.

I’m checking the source records, calculations and repository validators before pushing the two branches and opening the PRs.

All local checks now pass, including project records, session logs, the token-site build, six solenoid controls and four calorimeter audit controls. The R–Z figure has been visually checked.

The source audit also found an identifier contract worth checking before reuse: the ODD factories place modules numbered 1–16, while the readout allocates four bits to that field. The report flags this for native verification.

The staged check caught trailing spaces in Matplotlib’s generated SVG; my earlier whitespace check had missed the untracked file. I’m adding normalization to the renderer and correcting the figure before publishing.

The PRs are open: [#64 for the solenoid baseline](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/64) and [#65 for the calorimeter assessment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/65). Both target main, and a merge-tree check confirms that their scientific changes combine without conflicts. I’m finishing the delivery records and checking hosted CI.

PR #65 has passed hosted validation and the token-site check. PR #64’s token-site check has passed; its full validation job is still running. Both PRs are mergeable against main, and the final branches also combine without conflicts.

PR #64’s CI found a record-order issue: I inserted its entry before PR #4, which an existing historical-review test expects first. I’m preserving that ordering and rerunning the affected check. The solenoid physics controls passed.

## My request:
As of #64, can you estimate how much material that would add before the calorimeter and plot it (t/X0 vs eta).

As of #65, please add a high level description to the PR directly with an execute summary.

I’ll add a clearly labelled solenoid material estimate and a t/X₀-versus-η plot to #64, with assumptions for the winding, supports and cryostat. Since their composition and wall thicknesses are still open, I’ll include a range.

I’ll also put a high-level executive summary directly at the top of #65’s PR description.

The executive summary is now at the top of #65. For #64, the illustrative estimate is about **1.40 X₀ at η = 0**, rising to about **3.75 X₀ near |η| = 1.67** before rays start missing the finite coil.

I’m plotting the component contributions and lean/heavier scenarios. These use an ATLAS-calibrated cold-mass proxy and assumed aluminium vessel walls and shields.

The material plot now shows the cold mass, vessel and shield contributions, with the finite-end geometry included. The reference central breakdown is **1.13 X₀ cold mass + 0.225 X₀ vessel walls + 0.045 X₀ shields**.

Twelve controls pass, along with the record and artifact checks. I’m pushing the plot, assumptions and calculation to #64.

The plot and assumptions are pushed to #64, and #65’s executive summary is in place. The curve drops at larger |η| because rays miss the finite solenoid annuli; it excludes material in forward or local service routes.

Local validation passed. I’m checking the final hosted run.
PR #65’s checks are green. The final #64 run is validating the published material update at commit `4e44d7c`; its token-site check has passed. Both PRs remain mergeable and combine without conflicts.

65 was merged upstream - make a new push (will likely be a 66 then I suppose).

The #64 material update is pushed and all checks are green. I’ll fetch the merged main branch and open a calorimeter follow-up PR, carrying the executive summary into both the document and the new PR description.

[PR #66 is open](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/66) from the merged main branch. It adds the executive summary to DES-027 and the PR description, and records #65’s merge metadata. Local validation passed.

Created and pushed [PR #66](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/66) from merged main. The executive summary is now in both DES-027 and the PR description. Local checks passed; hosted validation is pending.

[PR #64](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/64) contains the material plot: **1.40 X₀ centrally**, with illustrative scenarios of **1.00–2.10 X₀**. Its CI is green.
